steps.body: On the number line the teens are the stretch between 10 and 20 — every teen sits its ones-count of steps past the ten.
steps.narration: On the number line the teens are the stretch between 10 and 20 — every teen sits its ones-count of steps past the ten.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 9. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 18 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 19.
20 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 9 hops from 10 to land on 19.

widget.missFeedback: Count 9 on from 10: you land on 19.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 9 more is 19 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 9 counts past ten are needed to reach 19.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 9 numbers, on 19.

predict.prompt: Where does 19 live on the line?
predict.reveal: The ones count the steps beyond the completed ten; teens all live to ten's right.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb teen line.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb teen line rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

commonLandings.feedback: 13 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 14.

widget.successFeedback: 10 and 4 more is 14 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 4 counts past ten are needed to reach 14.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 4 numbers, on 14.

widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — keep hopping back until you reach 14.

options.feedback: 15 is where we stood; the question asks for the number just before it.
13 skips a number; the count moves one at a time through the teens too.
16 comes AFTER 15; before means one step back.
Correct — the teens climb by ones, so stepping one back from 15 lands on 14.
